chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn 'Uzafir, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man has a debt upon another man, and the creditor delays (the debtor) until he (the creditor) dies, then the debtor reconciles with his inheritors upon something (a reduced amount), so that which the inheritors take is for them, and whatever remains is for the deceased until he is fulfilled from it in the Hereafter; and if he does not reconcile with them upon anything until he dies, and does not pay it off, then all of it is for the deceased to seize him (the debtor) with (in the Hereafter).
ai.seo_question: What happens to an unpaid debt if the creditor dies before it is settled?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'Haqq al-Mawta' (the right of the deceased) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that unpaid debts are not extinguished by death but persist as spiritual claims. It distinguishes between partial settlements with heirs, where the remainder remains a debt of the deceased, and total non-settlement, where the full amount is exacted in the Hereafter. This underscores the continuity of financial obligations beyond death, a key principle in Shia legal theory regarding inheritance and debt clearance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Uzafir, from Umar Bin Yazeed, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When there was a debt for a man upon a man, so he (debtor) delays it until he (the creditor) died, then (the debtor) reconciles with his inheritors upon something (for a lower amount to be paid), so that which the inheritors take possession of would be for them, and whatever remains from the (debt), so it is for the deceased until he may be fulfilled from it in the Hereafter; but if he does not reconcile with them upon something until he dies, and does not give (anything) from it, so all of it would be for the deceased to seize him (the borrower) with (in the Hereafter)’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma’il from Muhammad ibn ’Adhafir from ’Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

’If one owes a certain amount of debts to another person and he delays payment until the creditor dies and then he reaches a settlement with such person’s heirs whatever they receive belongs to them and the remaining belongs to the deceased who will acquire from him in the next life; but if he does not reach any settlement with the heirs of the deceased all of the loan belongs to the deceased for which the borrower will be held responsible.’”
